subject: science
passage: The hoatzin, a pheasant-sized bird of the swampy forests of South America, usually builds its nest on branches that hang over water. When a snake or other predator comes near, a young hoatzin may simply drop out of the nest into the water below and swim away. Once the danger has passed, the chick climbs back up to the nest, gripping the branches with two small claws on each wing. These claws disappear as the bird grows up.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Hoatzins build their nests over water so that predators cannot reach the eggs.
choices.B: Young hoatzins have a way to escape predators and then return to their nests.
choices.C: Adult hoatzins use the claws on their wings to climb through swampy forests.
choices.D: Snakes are the most common predators of birds in South American forests.

explanation.why: The text explains what a young hoatzin does when a predator comes near: it drops into the water and swims away, and later it climbs back to the nest using claws on its wings. The main idea must cover both parts of this survival strategy, escaping and returning.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says where hoatzins nest but never says the nests keep predators from reaching eggs.
explanation.B: Correct. This covers the whole text: the chick escapes by dropping into the water and then climbs back up with its wing claws.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the claws disappear as the bird grows up, so adults do not use them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text mentions a snake as one possible predator but never compares predators of forest birds.
